Variable Interest Entity FGMWC is a non-profit mutual benefit corporation under California law formed by the Company in 2010 and for which the Company manages all corporate functions. Under the Company’s water supply agreements, the Company expects to contribute its annual water supply from the Mojave Groundwater Bank to FGMWC. Participating public water agencies and other beneficiaries of water supply and storage rights will own shares in FGMWC under the class structure set forth in FGMWC’s bylaws. No participating public water agency currently owns shares in FGMWC. On July 14, 2026, the United States Bureau of Land Management (“BLM”) issued FGMWC a right-of-way grant under Title V of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act (“FLPMA ROW Grant”) authorizing the conversion of the Company’s 220 -mile 30” steel pipeline (the “Northern Pipeline”) to water conveyance on BLM-administered lands (see Note 7 – “Leases & Property, Plant, Equipment and Water Programs”). On July 27, 2026, FGMWC executed construction-manager-at-risk contracts establishing guaranteed maximum prices for the principal construction components of the Northern Pipeline conversion (see Note 10 – “Commitments and Contingencies”). In April 2026, FGMWC and the County of San Bernardino formed the San Bernardino Water and Power Authority ("SBWPA"), a joint powers authority. As of September 30, 2026 , FGMWC has not issued shares or membership interests and has no equity investment at risk; its activities, including the rent, fees and performance and reclamation bond required for the FLPMA ROW Grant and the costs of its construction contracts, are funded by the Company. FGMWC is therefore a VIE. The Company is FGMWC’s primary beneficiary because it manages FGMWC and directs the activities that most significantly affect its economic performance – obtaining the authorizations for and developing the Northern Pipeline conversion and contracting for water supply – and because it funds FGMWC and absorbs its losses. The Company has not guaranteed FGMWC’s obligations under the FLPMA ROW Grant or its construction contracts. Under its water delivery agreements, however, the Company has agreed to arrange and finance the capital costs of the Northern Pipeline conveyance facilities, on its own or in coordination with FGMWC or others. During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company funded FGMWC’s payment of $ 268,000 of initial rent and the $ 2.54 million cash performance and reclamation bond FGMWC deposited with BLM as required by the FLPMA ROW Grant. Cadiz Real Estate LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, is currently FGMWC’s sole member. The Company intends to continue funding FGMWC’s obligations under the FLPMA ROW Grant until FGMWC’s members assume them when water is available, and to fund FGMWC’s pre-construction costs and other obligations incurred before project financing for the Northern Pipeline conversion is obtained. Construction under FGMWC’s construction contracts will begin only upon satisfaction of the applicable financing conditions (see Note 10 – “Commitments and Contingencies”). The Company reassesses on an ongoing basis whether it is FGMWC’s primary beneficiary. Changes in FGMWC’s governing documents or equity, such as the issuance of membership interests to participating public water agencies, or in its activities, such as the contribution of the Northern Pipeline assets to Mojave Water Infrastructure Company LLC, would require the Company to reconsider whether FGMWC is a VIE. If the FLPMA ROW Grant were vacated (see Note 10 – “Commitments and Contingencies”), FGMWC would derecognize the related right-of-use asset and lease liability to the extent its rights and obligations under the grant ended.
